decisionsTitle: «Emailuri» as a column of the «Voluntari» and registrations lists: each person's three newest emails, for the Administrator (amending §915, §651 and §943)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-17**, on a phone, the morning after the volunteers were emailed their points (§956): «Vreau sa vad mai clar ce mailuri a primit fiecare om».

**What the backoffice said until now.** The answer was in two places and neither is at a glance. «Emailuri azi» (§912) is the day's emails grouped by the press that queued them, not by person. A person's own «Emailuri» (§915) is a closed fold on the person's page — the volunteer's, and inside the registration's «Emailuri» card — so «who got what» meant opening each person in turn. The owner's way all week has been the list: the person's message, the organizers' notes and the race-day decision each became a column of «Voluntari» («să știu direct», §947, §950, §954).

**Decision — a column, «Emailuri» / “Emails”, on both lists.** On «Voluntari» right after «Stare»; on the registrations list right after «Unde a ajuns». Each row says the person's three newest emails, one to a line — «{the email's name} · {when} · {what became of it}» — and under them, when there are more, «și încă N emailuri» / “and N more emails”, a link to the person's own «Emailuri» (`#emailuri`: the fold of the volunteer's page, §915, and the card of the registration's, §671), where every email stands with its tries and who caused it — a plain link, and that fold is open when the page is: the backoffice opens the fold an address names on arrival (`OpenFoldFromHash`, §336). A person with no email says «niciun email», in grey: an answer, not an absence, so the column has no `omitEmptyOnPhone` and a phone's card keeps the line. Its «?» says: «Ultimele trei emailuri ale persoanei: ce email, când a plecat sau de când așteaptă și ce s-a întâmplat cu el. Toate, cu detalii, sunt pe pagina persoanei.» It neither sorts nor filters.

- **The name** is the catalogue's (`emailTypeName`, `Admin.emails.types`): the owner reads «Punctul tău de voluntar», never `VOLUNTEER_POINT`.
- **The moment** is when the email left (`sent_at`) or, while it has not — waiting, failed, refused at the send — when it was queued; on the club's clock, in the lists' own short form with its year («mie., 21 oct. 2026, 12:30»), in lower case because it continues a line. Never «azi» or a bare hour: a list is read on other days than the email's.
- **The three newest are the newest by that moment**, so the hours of a cell never run backwards: an email held back (a role's two minutes, a send paced over an evening) and sent after a later one stands above it. The fold is ordered by the queueing its rows show first; the same emails, each screen in the order of the moment it shows.
- **What became of it** is one word of a closed set, below.
- **Drawn** by one cell, `notifications/ui/EmailSummary.tsx`: a Server Component, plain text and one plain anchor — no island, no client fetch, nothing to hydrate. The link is 44 pixels tall above its words (`INLINE_TAP_TARGET`), over the three lines that always stand above it when it is drawn; its accessible name begins with the words it shows and ends with the person's name (WCAG 2.5.3). The outcome is a quiet coloured word, not a chip: a chip is taller than a line, and three of them would push a phone's card. On the wide table the cell stands on a floor of sixteen rem — §943's lesson: a full table squeezes a column of wrapping words to its heading, a word to a line — where an email takes two lines (measured in a browser for «Detalii actualizate (loc, oră, program)», «Înscriere confirmată (cu QR și număr)» and «Declarația semnată (PDF atașat)», each with its moment and its word), and never past twenty-eight rem, which the backoffice's widest frame (1990 px) does not reach: there the column is 307 px with its padding, and an email still two lines. An email wraps on a phone's card as on the wide table — at 320 px each of three took three lines of the card's right-aligned value — so six pixels stand between two emails, not two, and each reads as one block; on the wide table the row is no taller for it (184 px on the browser spec's page, as with two).

**One judgement for what became of an email.** `notifications/domain/email-outcome.ts#emailOutcomeOf`, asked in this order: **waiting** (queued, or held by a worker: `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`), **failed** (it spent its tries and never left), **rejected** (the recipient's server refused it, or the person marked it as spam: `BOUNCED`, `COMPLAINED`), **captured** (the environment kept it — QA's allowlist, `recipient_count = 0`: it reached nobody), **delivered** (it left and the recipient's server took it, `delivered_at`), **sent** (it left and nothing more is known: no delivery fact yet, or a road that reports none). It was the fold's own, written out three times — in its chip (`EmailJournal.tsx#DepartedChip`), its waiting mark and its closed line (`EmailHistory.tsx`). Those three now ask the function and draw exactly what they drew, and the column asks it too, so a row can never read one way on the list and another on the person's page. A captured row never reads «Livrat», on the list or in the fold, whose dated «Livrat …» line asks the function as well: it reached nobody, so no server took it — and a `delivered_at` on such a row, which cannot happen in practice, would not change what it says.

**The words are the fold's.** «așteaptă», «eșuat», «refuzat» and «n-a ajuns la nimeni (QA)» are the closed line's own keys (`Admin.emails.history.last.*`), and «niciun email» is its `summaryNone`. The fold says a departure with its hour inside the words («a plecat la 10:15») and a delivery as a dated sentence («Livrat …», §671); the column says the moment beside the word, so those two got their bare forms beside them — `last.sent` «a plecat» / “left”, `last.delivered` «livrat» / “delivered”: the same words, never a second vocabulary («trimis», «expediat»), and a test holds each to the fold's sentence. One word of the brief was not taken: the English “no email” — the fold already says “no emails” of the same fact, and one fact keeps one sentence. New are only the column's own: `Admin.emails.summary.column`, `.hint` and `.more.{one,few,other}` («și încă 1 email», «… 3 emailuri», «… 20 de emailuri», by `countForm`, no ICU plural). The ink is the colour of the fold's chip: green for what left, amber for a refusal, red for a failure, grey for what waits or reached nobody — the word says the outcome, the colour only repeats it.

**Who: the fold's own people.** The Administrator and the Superadministrator alone, by the fold's own assertion (`email-history.ts#assertMayReadEmailHistory`, now exported — `canManageRegistrations`, the capability that gates «Emailuri azi»), asked in the reader before anything is read: every other role — the desk's Volunteer, the Redactor, the Organizer, the Tehnic role, a member — is refused FORBIDDEN, never handed an empty map that would read as «nobody got anything» (BR-REQ-060-01). The same people as the fold because the column is the fold in short: a list that showed what the person's page refuses would be two answers to one question, and §915 kept the Organizer's card without the tries on purpose. The pages add the column and call the reader for those two roles only; for the Organizer, who reads both lists, each list is exactly as it was and nothing is read.

**What is read, and what never is.** `notifications/email-summaries.ts#readEmailSummaries(db, actor, { registrationIds } | { volunteerIds })` answers a `Map` from each id to `{ total, lines: [{ id, messageType, at, outcome }] }`. Read: the type, the state, when it was queued and when it left, how many it reached, whether it was delivered. Of the payload only what names the row — the volunteer's id (the journal's expression, now exported as `journal.ts#VOLUNTEER_ID_OF_ROW`, of which `VOLUNTEER_OF_ROW` is built) and the club-copy flag. Never the payload's words, a body, a link, an address, `last_error`, the provider's code or words, who pressed. The club's side — a copy, the declaration's archive, a notice to the club's people — is neither counted nor drawn, by the very predicate the fold counts «N emailuri» with (`isClubSide` as SQL, exported as `email-history.ts#CLUB_SIDE_OF_ROW`): the list's three lines are three of the fold's own rows, and its «și încă N» the rest of the fold's count. On a registration's page that fold is «Încercări și cine le-a trimis», inside the card «Emailuri», whose heading counts every row the outbox holds for the registration, the club's copy and archive among them (§671): a registration with six emails of its own and two of the club's reads «și încă 3 emailuri» on the list, «6 emailuri» on the fold's closed line and «8 emailuri» beside the card's title. That heading is §671's, read by every role that reads the page, and is left as it was. The guard reads the statement PostgreSQL is sent: every name in it is the table, one of nine of its columns or one of the statement's own four, and the payload is asked for those two keys and nothing else.

**One query a page.** The three newest and the count of each person are computed in the statement itself (`row_number()` and `count(*)` over the person), so the answer is at most three rows a person whatever they have been sent; no statement at all for a page with no rows, and none for a role that is refused. Registrations are found by `registration_id` (`email_outbox_registration_created_idx`, the index of the registration's own «Emailuri»). Volunteers are found by the id their payload names, which no index holds: one pass over the outbox each time a page of «Voluntari» is drawn for the Administrator — what a volunteer's fold costs once for one person (§915), paid here on every view of the list — and no migration while the outbox is small; an expression index on that key is the remedy the day it is not. Narrowing the pass to the types that carry a volunteer's id was left out: no one list names them — the volunteer's own five, the parent's link and the colleagues' notice are queued from four modules — the fold reads without one, and a type a second list forgot would make the column's count disagree with the fold's; with no index on the type it would still be one pass over the outbox, only with fewer payloads opened. Ids that are not uuids are dropped before the statement, an id asked twice is asked once, and at most 200 people are asked about in one call — twice the lists' largest page — the rest getting no entry rather than a false «none». The reader takes no clock: nothing it answers depends on one, and an argument nothing reads was left out. It only reads: no write, no cache tag.

**What it costs on the screen, said plainly.**

- **The registrations table does not fit the owner's 1858-px screen whole while the column is drawn — and no width of the column would make it.** §943 left that list fitting there and wrote the rule into its browser test: a column added there fits, or leaves below a breakpoint; and §943 itself refused hiding columns by breakpoint: what to give up is «Coloane»'s question. Measured in a browser on that screen (1858 × 900, a production build of this change; the frame 1808 px). On a page of a race's usual states — five registrations: an address not confirmed yet, a declaration owed, an offer open, a place on the waiting list and a confirmed place, each with its five emails — the list's other columns take 1722 px at their least (§943 measured 1734 for one event's list), «Stare» holding «Așteaptă confirmarea emailului» on one line: 86 px are left, and the column needs 108 even where it says only «niciun email» — its heading and its «?». On its floor, 280 px with its padding, that table is 2002 px, **194 px wider than its frame**, and scrolls sideways under the pinned verbs, as the every-event list has since §943 (142 px). The browser spec's own page, one confirmed registration, is narrower — 1871 px, 63 wider — and fits with nobody on it emailed. **A lower floor was measured and buys no fit**, so the floor stays at sixteen rem: from fifteen rem down to nine, twelve fits the one-registration page by 1 px and ten by 33, while the page of the usual states stays 82 to 178 px too wide; and below fifteen rem the emails start taking three lines — at fourteen two of the three, at twelve all three — so the row grows from 184 px to 218, then 238: taller, and still wider than its frame. Leaving the year out of this year's moments («lun., 16 nov., 10:58») was measured too: at sixteen rem an email is two lines either way, and the year saves a line only at floors that do not fit; the moment keeps the lists' own form, year and all. A row with three emails is taller than it was in any case: 184 px where it was 116. The column is drawn by default all the same, because the owner asked to see each person's emails at a glance. **To have the whole table on that screen again, open «Coloane», at the right end of the table's headings, and untick «Emailuri»**: that browser remembers it, the table fits exactly as before, and ticking it brings the column back. `tests/e2e/admin-column-widths.spec.ts` does both on that screen with the row emailed: drawn, the verbs stay whole in the frame and the page never scrolls sideways; unticked, it asks what §943 asked. The floors and the page of the usual states were measured by a probe in the same browser, not kept in the suite: the spec holds the rule, not the figures.
- **«Până când» is no longer right beside the step for the Administrator** (§651): «Unde a ajuns», then the step's emails, then its deadline. For the Organizer the two stand side by side as before.
- **§915 left «a count of emails or tries on the registrations list» out** because that list's query is the hot page's. That query is untouched: this is one more read over the same index, for the two roles alone.

**Not done, on purpose.**

- **Filtering or sorting a list by an email** — «who did NOT get X». A different question with a query of its own; the column answers «what did this person get».
- **The column for the Organizer.** §915's rule stays: a person's emails are the Administrators'.
- **The Excel and CSV files.** They are handed to people outside the backoffice; an email's trail is no column of a participant list.
- **«Emailuri azi», the plan's page and the person's own fold**: unchanged in what they draw. The fold stays the whole story, with the tries and the causes.
- **A cell on an invitation's row** of the registrations list: an invitation is no registration, and its emails hang on none.
- **The tries, the cause, a refusal's reason, a chip an outcome** in the cell: three lines stay three lines, and the rest is one tap away.
- **A column hidden until it is ticked.** «Coloane» hides only what a person unticked (§661); a column hidden from the start would be a change to every list's menu and its pre-paint script, for a column the owner asked to see.
- **A migration or a dependency**: none.

**Tested.** `tests/integration/notifications/email-summaries.test.ts` (PGlite): the five other roles refused for both kinds of subject with no statement sent; registrations and volunteers each their own rows and nobody else's, a registration's id and a volunteer's never answering for each other; the club's rows neither counted nor drawn; the three newest by the moment each shows — an email held back standing above a later one — and the total, equal to the fold's count; every outcome; malformed, repeated and upper-case ids; one statement a page and none for nobody; the cap; every statement a `SELECT` and the outbox left as it was; the statement's names and the payload's two keys. `tests/unit/notifications/email-outcome.test.ts` holds the judgement over every state a row can be in and refuses a state named in the column's reader or cell; `email-outcome-words.test.ts` draws the fold's chip, its closed line and the column's word for every such state and compares them. `tests/integration/volunteers/emails-column.test.ts` (the page as the server streams it) and `tests/integration/registrations/emails-column.test.ts` (the page's table and its cells), in Romanian and in English: the column's place, heading and «?»; a person's lines, «și încă N» in its counted forms with its link and the person's name, «niciun email», in the table and on a phone's card; six pixels between two emails; one read a page; the anchors; and for the Organizer no column, the other columns in the same order, the reader never called. `row-deadline-column.test.ts` says where «Până când» stands for each role. In a browser, run on both projects against a production build of this change: `tests/e2e/admin-column-widths.spec.ts`, whose registration now has five emails — at 1000 px, with the column drawn, the last column still stands whole beside the pinned verbs and a press there is scrolled clear of them; at 1858 px the cell draws its three lines and «și încă 2 emailuri» on its floor, the verbs stay whole in the frame, the page never scrolls sideways, and «Emailuri» unticked gives back §943's fit; at 320 px the card carries the three lines without the page scrolling sideways, and «și încă 2 emailuri» lands on the registration's «Emailuri» open.

Amends §915 (a person's emails are also a column of the two lists; its «left out» of the registrations list), §651 (where «Până când» stands for the Administrator) and §943 (the fit on the owner's screen holds with «Emailuri» unticked).
changelogLine: - **«Emailuri» on the «Voluntari» and registrations lists** — for an Administrator a column says each person's three newest emails: which email, when it left and what became of it («așteaptă», «a plecat», «livrat», «refuzat», «eșuat»), then «și încă N emailuri» to the person's own «Emailuri», open, and «niciun email» for somebody never emailed; the Organizer's lists are as before. With the column drawn, the registrations table is wider than a 1858-px screen and scrolls under its pinned verbs; unticking «Emailuri» under «Coloane» fits it again. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the lists' «Emailuri» column (`readEmailSummaries`, for a page of registrations or of volunteers), when anyone but an Administrator or a Superadministrator asks for it — the desk's Volunteer, the Redactor, the Organizer, the Tehnic role, a member — then the server refuses with FORBIDDEN before any statement is sent, never an empty answer; and neither the registrations list nor the «Voluntari» list draws the column or calls the reader for them, so the Organizer's lists are exactly as before (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the registrations list, when an Administrator or a Superadministrator opens it, then a column «Emailuri» / “Emails” right after «Unde a ajuns», with its «?», in the table and on a phone's card, says each registration's three newest own emails, one to a line and the newest first — the email's name as «Emailuri» names it, the moment it left or, while it has not, was queued (the club's clock, the list's short form with its year; the lines are ordered by it) and what became of it in the fold's words: «așteaptă», «a plecat», «livrat», «refuzat», «eșuat», «n-a ajuns la nimeni (QA)» — then, when there are more, «și încă N emailuri» («1 email», «3 emailuri», «20 de emailuri»), a link a thumb reaches (44 pixels tall above its words) to the registration's «Emailuri» (`#emailuri`), named for the person and landing on that card open, and «niciun email» for a registration with none; the club's copy and archive are neither counted nor drawn, a test registration's row is drawn like any other, and «Până când» follows the column (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The «Emailuri» column costs one statement a page of people — each person's three newest emails and their count computed in it — and none for a page with no rows; an id that is not a uuid never reaches the database, at most 200 people are asked about in one call, and the statement names only the email's type, its state, when it was queued and when it left, how many it reached and whether it was delivered, and of the payload only the volunteer's id and the club-copy flag — never an address, a body, a link, `last_error` or the provider's words; it writes nothing (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

What became of an email is one judgement (`emailOutcomeOf`): waiting while it is queued or held, failed once its tries are spent, rejected when the recipient's server refused it or the person marked it as spam, captured when the environment kept it (`recipient_count = 0`), delivered when the recipient's server took it, sent otherwise; the fold's chip, its waiting mark and its closed line and the lists' column all ask it, so a row never reads one way on a list and another on the person's page (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 15 in where the column stands. Given the registrations list, then for an Administrator or a Superadministrator «Emailuri» stands between «Unde a ajuns» and «Până când» — the step, its emails, its deadline — and for the Organizer, who has no «Emailuri», «Până când» stays right after «Unde a ajuns» (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 23's last clause. Given the registrations list with one event chosen on a 1858-px screen, then the whole table fits its frame, nothing scrolling sideways, once the Administrator's «Emailuri» is unticked under «Coloane» (remembered in that browser); with «Emailuri» drawn a table wider than its frame scrolls inside it under the pinned verbs, which stay whole in the frame, and the page itself never scrolls sideways (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the «Voluntari» list, when an Administrator or a Superadministrator opens it, then a column «Emailuri» / “Emails” right after «Stare», with its «?», in the table and on a phone's card, says each volunteer's three newest emails as the registrations list says a registration's — the rows whose payload names the volunteer, their parent's link among them, the colleagues' notice and the club's copies never — then «și încă N emailuri» to the volunteer's own «Emailuri» fold (`#emailuri`) and «niciun email» for a volunteer never emailed, read once for the page's rows; the Organizer's list has no such column (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: «Emailuri» as a column of the «Voluntari» and registrations lists: each person's three newest emails, for the Administrator
